items.label: f03-bulkheads
items.front: How does the worker keep one bad link from sinking a whole batch, and where is backpressure missing?
items.back: Per-link try/catch in archiveLink, per-feed try/catch in RSS polling, and Promise.allSettled over each batch. Batch sizes are capped (ARCHIVE_TAKE_COUNT, INDEX_TAKE_COUNT), but RSS fan-out uses an unbounded Promise.all.

items.label: f02-auth-chain
items.front: What does Linkwarden's authentication chain check, in order?
items.back: verifyToken: decode the NextAuth JWT, check the user id, a manual exp check, then a jti revocation lookup in AccessToken. verifyUser: the user exists, has a username, has a verified email (if enabled) and a subscription (if Stripe).

items.label: f01-marker-columns
items.front: Name the idempotency marker columns Linkwarden uses, one per side effect.
items.back: lastPreserved (archiving), indexVersion (Meilisearch indexing), aiTagged (AI tagging), trialEndEmailSent (trial-end email). Each loop checks its column before acting: make the completion of an effect queryable.

items.prompt: Inside archiveHandler, page.goto throws partway through archiving a link. What does the finally block write to that link's row?

choices.text: It deletes the link row, since no archive of it could be produced
It stamps lastPreserved and marks each missing format unavailable
It leaves lastPreserved null, so the next pass tries the link again
It bumps a retry counter, then backs off before trying it again

choices: It deletes the link row, since no archive of it could be produced
It stamps lastPreserved and marks each missing format unavailable
It leaves lastPreserved null, so the next pass tries the link again
It bumps a retry counter, then backs off before trying it again

items.explanation: The finally block runs on success and failure alike: if the row still exists it sets lastPreserved to now and every empty format to "unavailable", so a failing URL is not retried.

items.prompt: updateLinkById receives a new, valid URL for an existing link. When are the old archive files deleted?

choices.text: Before the Prisma update of the link row runs
Later, when the worker archives the new URL
Not at all; they stay until the link is deleted
After the update commits, in a post-commit hook

choices: Before the Prisma update of the link row runs
Later, when the worker archives the new URL
Not at all; they stay until the link is deleted
After the update commits, in a post-commit hook

items.explanation: When data.url differs from oldLink.url and is valid, removeFiles(oldLink.id, oldLink.collectionId) runs, and only afterwards prisma.link.update. If the update fails, the files are already gone.

items.prompt: A client calls GET /api/v1/links?sort=abc. What value does the route pass to getLinks as sort?

choices.text: none; the route answers with 400 for an invalid sort value
undefined, because the route drops the invalid value
NaN, because Number(...) of the text is passed on unchecked
0, the default sort that is used when the parse fails

choices: none; the route answers with 400 for an invalid sort value
undefined, because the route drops the invalid value
NaN, because Number(...) of the text is passed on unchecked
0, the default sort that is used when the parse fails

items.explanation: The route builds convertedData with sort: Number(req.query.sort as string) and no check; Number("abc") is NaN. The validation map calls this manual coercion a known gap.

items.prompt: How often does linkProcessing replace its Playwright browser even when nothing has gone wrong?

choices.text: Once a day, on the first loop pass after midnight
Only when the browser reports that it has been disconnected
After every batch of 5 links, the ARCHIVE_TAKE_COUNT
Every 30 minutes, checked at the top of each loop pass

choices: Once a day, on the first loop pass after midnight
Only when the browser reports that it has been disconnected
After every batch of 5 links, the ARCHIVE_TAKE_COUNT
Every 30 minutes, checked at the top of each loop pass

items.explanation: The loop compares Date.now() - browserStartTs with BROWSER_MAX_AGE_MS (30 minutes) and calls restartBrowser("30-minute rotation"). A disconnect also triggers a restart, but it is not the only trigger.

items.prompt: A user deletes a link while the worker is still archiving it. What does the finally block in archiveHandler do?

choices.text: It marks the formats unavailable on a tombstone row instead
It throws, and the supervisor restarts the whole worker
It recreates the row, so that the finished archive is kept
It finds the row gone, so it removes the files it just wrote

choices: It marks the formats unavailable on a tombstone row instead
It throws, and the supervisor restarts the whole worker
It recreates the row, so that the finished archive is kept
It finds the row gone, so it removes the files it just wrote

items.explanation: finally re-reads the link with findUnique; when it is gone (finalLink is null) it calls removeFiles(link.id, link.collectionId), a compensation step for files written mid-archive.

items.prompt: In linkIndexing, the waitForTask call for a batch rejects with a timeout. What happens to the indexVersion of those links?

choices.text: It is set to null, so the archive worker redoes those links
The loop throws, and the worker restarts that batch later
They get the current version anyway; the error is just logged
It stays stale, so the next pass sends the same batch again

choices: It is set to null, so the archive worker redoes those links
The loop throws, and the worker restarts that batch later
They get the current version anyway; the error is just logged
It stays stale, so the next pass sends the same batch again

items.explanation: waitForTask(...).catch only logs the error; the code then runs prisma.link.updateMany setting indexVersion to MEILI_INDEX_VERSION for every id in the batch. The guide row says rows stay stale until success; that holds for an addDocuments failure, not for a waitForTask error.

items.prompt: getPermission({ userId, linkId }) is called for a link in a collection the user has no relation to. What does it return?

choices.text: null, as the query filters on the owner or on a member of it
An empty members list, so the other users stay hidden
The collection with its members; the caller applies the rule
A 401 response object that the route can return directly

choices: null, as the query filters on the owner or on a member of it
An empty members list, so the other users stay hidden
The collection with its members; the caller applies the rule
A 401 response object that the route can return directly

items.explanation: The linkId branch queries collection.findFirst({ where: { links: { some: { id: linkId } } }, include: { members: true } }) and never uses userId. It returns relationship data; each controller decides.

items.prompt: The worker.ts process crashes on an uncaught error. In this repo, what brings the worker loops back?

choices.text: PM2, which the worker package uses as its process runner
The web app, which starts a worker on its next API request
Nothing; links stay unpreserved until someone restarts it by hand
apps/worker/index.ts spawns it again with tsx after 5 seconds

choices: PM2, which the worker package uses as its process runner
The web app, which starts a worker on its next API request
Nothing; links stay unpreserved until someone restarts it by hand
apps/worker/index.ts spawns it again with tsx after 5 seconds

items.explanation: index.ts spawns tsx worker.ts as a child and, on exit, logs and calls setTimeout(launch, 5000). The worker package scripts run tsx index.ts; the web worker route only reports stats.

items.prompt: archiveHandler marks a link as preserved even when archiving it failed. What reason does the side-effects guide give for that choice?

choices.text: Because Prisma cannot store a failed state on a link row
Because the Wayback copy already preserves the failed page
So that a poison URL is not archived over and over
Because indexing waits for lastPreserved before it runs

choices: Because Prisma cannot store a failed state on a link row
Because the Wayback copy already preserves the failed page
So that a poison URL is not archived over and over
Because indexing waits for lastPreserved before it runs

items.explanation: Archiving is at most once on purpose: duplicate indexing is harmless, but re-archiving a URL that always fails or hangs would waste the worker forever. A failed link is stored as unavailable formats, the Wayback call is fire-and-forget, and indexing selects on indexVersion, not lastPreserved.

items.prompt: A collection member with canUpdate edits a link and sets its collection to another collection they also belong to. What does updateLinkById do?

choices.text: Refuses with a 401, since moving links is for owners
Moves it, provided the member has canCreate there
Moves it, since canUpdate covers the collection field
Refuses with a 403, the usual authorization status

choices: Refuses with a 401, since moving links is for owners
Moves it, provided the member has canCreate there
Moves it, since canUpdate covers the collection field
Refuses with a 403, the usual authorization status

items.explanation: isCollectionOwner is false and the target id differs from the current collection, so unauthorizedSwitchCollection is true and the controller returns 401 "You can't move a link to/from a collection you don't own." The repo uses 401 for authorization denials.

items.prompt: A session JWT is not expired, but its AccessToken row has revoked: true. What does verifyToken give back?

choices.text: A freshly issued token, after rotating the revoked jti value
The string saying the session expired, so the request is refused
A status object with 403, the code for a revoked credential
The decoded token, since its signature and exp claim are both valid

choices: A freshly issued token, after rotating the revoked jti value
The string saying the session expired, so the request is refused
A status object with 403, the code for a revoked credential
The decoded token, since its signature and exp claim are both valid

items.explanation: After the exp check, verifyToken looks up accessToken.findFirst({ token: token.jti, revoked: true }); a hit returns "Your session has expired, please log in again." instead of the token.

items.prompt: The archiving loop runs every few seconds. What stops it from archiving the same link again on every pass?

choices.text: The batch query picks just the links whose lastPreserved is null
A unique index on Link.url that rejects any repeated work
An archived flag that the web app sets when it serves a link
A per-link Redis lock that is taken before archiving starts

choices: The batch query picks just the links whose lastPreserved is null
A unique index on Link.url that rejects any repeated work
An archived flag that the web app sets when it serves a link
A per-link Redis lock that is taken before archiving starts

items.explanation: getLinkBatchFairly selects links with url not null and lastPreserved: null, and archiveHandler always stamps lastPreserved in its finally block. That column is the pipeline's idempotency key.
